title: Convoy TAKA-206, 22–23 November 1944
eyebrow: East of Formosa · Coordinated attack group "Sandy's Sluggers", Cdr L. D. McGregor in REDFISH

participants.name: REDFISH
participants.co: Cdr L. D. McGregor, pack commander

participants.name: SHAD
participants.co: L. Julihn (middle initial illegible on the report)

paras.text: The three boats' torpedo attacks of 22–23 November 1944, as typed on their attack sheets, beside the log the convoy's minesweeper W-15 kept of the same night. Times are converted to GMT, so BANG and SHAD (zone K) and the Japanese escorts (zone I) share one clock.

Three of the six ships were sunk (Hozan, Amakusa and Sakae Maru); Taiken, Sannin and Eikai Maru sheltered at Funauki (W-15's signal log). BANG claimed four sunk and one damaged; REDFISH two sunk (her Attacks 1 and 3, 0104 and 0141 K); SHAD's one salvo, fired by mistake at a torpedo boat at 2338 K, missed. The postwar credit gives BANG Sakae and Amakusa Maru and REDFISH Hozan Maru, but W-15 logged Hozan Maru torpedoed at 2339 I (0039 K), 25 minutes before REDFISH first fired and seven minutes after BANG's Attack 1.
Keelung to Naha, sailed 22 November; ships and escorts from W-15's battle report. The convoy's own record: [[convoy:taka-206]].
Positions are each navigator's own dead reckoning; lines between them are straight. REDFISH's chronology position for Hozan Maru (24-27N 122-47E) is her own Attack 3 position, not the target's.

BANG, REDFISH and SHAD all kept zone K (−10) that night (the pack agreed "all times ... will be minus ten (King)"). Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9): Manazuru's red flare at 2240 I is 2340 K, 52 minutes before BANG's Attack 1.

REDFISH heard "first of many explosions; BANG apparently made her attack" at 0037 K and fired her own first torpedoes at 0104 K. W-15 saw Hozan Maru torpedoed at 2339 I (0039 K). By the reports' own clocks the hit fits BANG's attack, not REDFISH's; the US credit to REDFISH appears to rest on her Attack 1 or 3 claim.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752: BANG Patrol 4 (74802868), REDFISH Patrol 2 (74837267, 74837338), SHAD Patrol 8 (74848165). Minesweeper W-15's battle report on TAKA-206 via JACAR (C08030607900, National Institute for Defense Studies). Which ships sank, from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

outcome.note: BANG fired at one medium AK at 2332 I from 2350 yds and saw it disappear; a ship was sunk at 2337 I 3.5 nm away (J03) and Hozan Maru was seen torpedoed at 2339 I (J02). The US Navy chronology gives Hozan Maru to REDFISH; REDFISH's report would settle it

Of TAKA-206's six ships, three were sunk (Hozan, Amakusa, Sakae Maru) and three reached Funauki (J04). BANG claimed four sunk and one damaged in seven attacks; the postwar credit is two (Sakae, Amakusa)

paras.text: Keelung to Naha, sailing at 0800 on 22 November 1944 with six ships and four escorts (W-15's battle report, p32–33). Three were sunk that night (Hozan, Amakusa and Sakae Maru); the other three sheltered at Funauki (Iriomote) on the 23rd. BANG, REDFISH and SHAD all attacked it (engagement `bang-patrol-4`).
**Cargo: not recorded** in W-15's report. The table gives each ship a type letter (A or C, not explained on the page), a top speed and a displacement.
